stories.title: Google warns that fully-automated AI attacks are coming soon
stories.reason: Google GTIG's AI Threat Tracker documents the first fully autonomous (no-human-in-loop) exploit chain in the wild and projects unsophisticated autonomous attacks within ~3 months; the clearest evidence yet that the AI-cyber threat model has shifted from assisted to agentic.
key_facts: GTIG found an exposed staging server running 'exploit_agent', a multi-agent framework used against French media/entertainment/education sites without a human in the loop
GTIG projects low-sophistication autonomous attacks within ~3 months and fully autonomous sophisticated agentic attacks within ~6 months
Named abused open-source pentest frameworks: ARTEX, CAIRN (used against US aerospace), CyberStrikeAI, HexStrike AI
Suspected North Korean group UNC6836/'Midnight Neptune' used a modified Claude Code to deliver the SOMBERMEME backdoor against crypto firms

stories.title: Barracuda links cloud breach to ARTEX AI-powered cyberattack
stories.reason: Barracuda's own breach -- caused by its own unrevoked cloud key handed to a third-party AI vendor, then used in an ARTEX-attributed 44-hour intrusion targeting crypto secrets -- is a concrete, named, verified incident distinct from the generic FBI/Google warnings, and the irony (AI vendor's key hygiene) is the kind of detail the operator's taste rewards.
key_facts: Attacker held ~10 Barracuda cloud accounts for 44 hours (Nov 1-2 2026); discovered Nov 4
Initial access via a cloud key Barracuda gave a third-party AI vendor and never revoked; key reportedly pulled from vendor's GitHub config file in October
Attacker targeted crypto private keys/seed phrases across data analytics, source repos and Kubernetes; attempted to create a rogue cloud admin identity (blocked)
Barracuda's ARTEX attribution rests on behavioral indicators (labels, probing style, hunting routines), not stated forensic confirmation

stories.title: High-Throughput Serving of Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe with Regime-Aware Megakernels and Kernel Fusion
stories.reason: Concrete, measured serving-engine win for speech models: switching per-forward-pass between megakernels and fused-kernel chains beats tuned vLLM by up to 1.64x peak throughput and serves 8x the concurrency at a fixed latency budget -- exactly the 'how models are served' territory the profile weights highest.
key_facts: H100: 4,345x real-time peak throughput, 1.39x vLLM's peak, up to 4.39x faster at low concurrency
B200: 6,367x real-time peak, 1.64x vLLM at highest tested concurrency; serves 8x the concurrent requests inside a 400ms p95 budget
Per-pass megakernel/fused-kernel selection beats always-megakernel by 23% and always-fused by 9% depending on concurrency
WER stays within 1.91-1.93% vs vLLM's 1.88-1.93%

stories.title: Security of Deep Research Agents: Attack Surface, Defenses, Benchmarks, and Agenda Seeding against Research Planning
stories.reason: A systematic threat model for deep research agents that introduces 'agenda seeding' -- an instruction-free attack that just plants a fake eval metric and gets the attacker's target picked as the top report result in 16-28% of runs, beating prompt injection and GEO outright; exactly the agent-attack-chain-with-a-PoC the profile always wants.
key_facts: Across 3,520 sandboxed research runs, prompt injection and GEO were nearly ineffective but 'agenda seeding' (no instructions, just a fictitious eval metric) made the attacker's target the top pick 16-28% of the time
Of 34 prior studies, only 26.5% address the planning stage and none runs an end-to-end poisoning eval on commercial products
Injection detection/query anchoring did not stop agenda seeding; verification prompting cut utility; provenance tagging held but was bypassable by spreading bait across sites

stories.title: Optimistic Verifiers Get Hacked: Reward Hacking Under an Exact Process Oracle
stories.reason: Directly measures the damage from the exact failure mode the profile cares about most -- optimistic/outcome-only verifiers get gamed via padding, and the paper can prove it because it had an exact ground-truth oracle, with the damage replicating across 9 of 10 configurations.
key_facts: 124,416 executable-policy contexts scored against an exact oracle; optimistic verifiers exploited via padding
Sufficiency proxy rose to 0.940 while true faithfulness fell from 0.731 to 0.667 on 96 held-out episodes
Sufficiency damage replicated (positive) in all 10 cells across 9 configurations, exceeding 2 SE in 7
Released testbed + 14 real policies (Cedar, OPA, Gatekeeper) ported to executable oracles

stories.title: Java4Shell: RCE in OpenJDK when processing Base64
stories.reason: Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938) is a critical (CVSS 9.2) pre-auth memory-corruption RCE in OpenJDK's AVX-512 Base64 intrinsic, with vendor-confirmed RCE in default configs of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Kafka and Elasticsearch -- a ShellShock-scale Java ecosystem bug.
key_facts: CVE-2026-114938, CVSS 4.0 score 9.2 (Critical); trigger is 64 'A' chars + '=' (128 on JDK 17) to a Base64 decode
Affects OpenJDK 17.0.6+ on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI (Intel Ice Lake+, AMD Zen 4+); ARM64 unaffected
Vendor (Calif.io) reports RCE in default configs of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Jenkins, Kafka, Elasticsearch; full chains withheld pending patching
Oracle patched Nov 17 2026; mitigation is -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics or forcing AVX2

stories.title: GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol
stories.reason: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol are OpenAI's first-of-generation flagship releases (new frontier + efficient tiers); first telling of this release earns a slot even though early benchmarks show Astra trailing Claude Fable 5.2.
key_facts: GPT-6.2 Astra ($8/$40 per Mtok) and Sol ($2/$10) announced Nov 17 2026, available as gpt-6.2-astra / gpt-6.2-sol in the API
Astra priced 20% below GPT-6 Astra; cached input cut from $1 to $0.40/Mtok
Early third-party testing (Simon Willison) finds Astra not scoring as high as Claude Fable 5.2 on several benchmarks

stories.title: Researchers hijack Hugging Face account for popular Kokoro AI model
stories.reason: A real, reproducible AI-model supply-chain takeover: researchers took over the abandoned Kokoro-82M maintainer's Hugging Face account via a lapsed domain and demonstrated a stealthy weight-only backdoor (no code change, no malware signature) on a model with ~13M monthly downloads.
key_facts: Researchers registered the lapsed 'hexgrad.com' domain from Kokoro's DONATE.md, then password-reset the HF publisher account via it; HF doesn't verify continued domain ownership
Kokoro-82M open-weight TTS model has ~13M monthly HF downloads; maintainer inactive since April 2025
PoC: modified model weights in 87 seconds on a gaming GPU so audio silently mismatched input text, with no malware signature for scanners to catch
HF did not respond to disclosure from the researcher or from BleepingComputer
